summary: Postinstall silently enables RDP, disables NLA, and enables session shadowing on Windows hosts
details: On `npm install`, the package's postinstall hook runs `node bin/biklimaster.js install --postinstall`, which triggers a UAC prompt and, upon approval, materially weakens the installer's Windows host security posture. It installs bundled unsigned Windows binaries (RDP Wrapper / RDPWInst.exe patching termsrv.dll), writes registry values enabling RDP, sets `UserAuthentication=0` (disabling Network Level Authentication), sets `Shadow=2` in both `HKLM\...\WinStations\RDP-Tcp` and the machine shadow policy (enabling full session shadowing without user consent), pins RDP to port 3389, and opens inbound firewall rules for TCP/UDP 3389 on the Any profile (including public networks). The net effect at install time is the installer's machine being converted into a remotely reachable, NLA-less RDP host with covert session-shadow capability enabled — a persistent remote-access backdoor configuration installed under a single UAC prompt on `npm install`, well outside anything a caller of an npm package would knowingly consent to.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
